result.title: A Benchmark for Spatially Grounded Gesture Generation
result.comment: 13 pages, 9 figures. Benchmark of the Referential Gesture Challenge at the HSI Workshop, ECCV 2026. Data and video: https://huggingface.co/datasets/hsi-workshop/referential-gesture-challenge
result.summary: Communication in shared space interweaves verbal and non-verbal signals, and pointing gestures anchor language to the environment: "put the cup on that one" is uninterpretable without the gesture that fixes the referent. Yet no common framework exists for evaluating whether generated gestures indicate their intended referent; distributional metrics reward a gesture aimed at the wrong object as long as it looks natural. We introduce a benchmark for spatially grounded gesture generation, comprising ~2K pointing-annotated clips from naturalistic VR dialogue with ground-truth 3D referents, a task in which systems must decide when, how and where to point within conversational speech, and a protocol that separates temporal alignment, spatial grounding and perceived naturalness. We also provide a flow-matching baseline, MM-Conv-Flow. Evaluating it alongside an independent retrieval-based system and captured human motion, we find that geometric grounding can exceed that of human pointing without any gain in perceived naturalness, showing that referential gesture quality must be measured along separate dimensions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出空间锚定手势生成基准，包含约 2K 段带指向标注的自然 VR 对话片段与 3D 指称真值，并给出分离时间对齐、空间锚定与感知自然度的评测协议及 flow-matching 基线 MM-Conv-Flow。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「指向何时、指向何物、指向何处」拆成独立维度评价的做法，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、STOP/LOOK 决策解耦评估有概念联系，方法线索可核查但尚属远领域启发。
